newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end higher, Clal Israel surges.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end higher, Clal Israel surges.

text.p: Israeli shares closed slightly higher on Sunday led by a sharp rise in Clal Israel and amid selective trading, traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of top 100 shares rose 0.41 percent, or 1.07 points, to 259.26 on all-share turnover of 175 million shekels against 183 million shekels on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.18 percent higher at 268.10.
Clal Israel surged 5.5 percent to 111 agorot and led the most actives on volume of 21.5 million shekels. Traders said there was no evident reason for the rise.
"Trading was very mixed and selective today. The market is finally behaving normally, with some shares rising and others falling," said Ron Weisberg of IBI Investment House.
He said investors are now focusing on the small capitalisation shares traded on the Caram index.

"Overall, trading was very quiet today and the market was stable. But activity continues to be relatively brisk and the market is showing strength," said Danniella Finn, head of sales at Batucha Securities and Investments.
"I believe that in the near future the market will stabilize and it even might decline slightly, but in the long run the trend is positive," Weisberg added.
Finn concurred. "We believe that the positive momentum will continue during the whole year," she said. "Investors are very optimistic. We haven't seen such a rise since 1994."

Among the losers, Israel Discount Bank plunged 4.0 percent to 398 agorot. On Thursday Israel's parliamentary finance committee gave the go-ahead for a secondary offering later this month of a 17 percent stake in the Bank.
The government hopes to raise a minimum of 600 million shekels from the offering, 28 percent from the share tranches and the remainder from the warrants.
But based on Discount's current market value, the offering is worth about 675 million shekels. Traders said the share fell as the market regards the minimum price is too low.

Other active shares included Bank Leumi, which closed unchanged at 526 agorot on volume of 6.2 million shekels, and Israel Chemicals which lost 0.75 percent to 396 agorot on turnover of 5.7 million shekels.
